extracted.intended_audience: individual authors (academic or independent) applying to NEH Public Scholars book grants
extracted.subtask_short: NEH Public Scholars book grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the NEH Public Scholars program (individual grants to support research and writing of well‑researched nonfiction books for general readers). Includes eligibility, required attachments, formatting, and the review criteria reviewers will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 1: Appeal and intellectual significance for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal and intellectual significance of the proposed book for general readers (corresponds to “Appeal and Significance,” “Sources and organization,” and “Final product and dissemination” sections of the narrative, as well as the writing sample and letters of reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe why the topic will interest a general audience and why it matters; summarize scope and basic ideas/questions/events/texts/people to be explored; relate to previous work and explain the new contribution; describe final product(s), audiences, dissemination and marketing plans; explain documentation and balance of readability vs thoroughness. Narrative and writing sample should show accessibility and broad appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 2: Applicant’s record and ability to interpret humanities for general audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s record of research and experience in interpreting the humanities for general audiences (corresponds to the “Competencies, skills, and access” section of the narrative, as well as the résumé and letters of reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain competence in the project area and experience conveying scholarship to broad audiences; list relevant positions, education, publications, awards on résumé; specify language or technical skills and access arrangements (archives/interviews); letters of reference should speak to these qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 3: Quality of conception, organization, and underlying humanities research
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project; and the breadth and depth of the humanities research underlying the project (corresponds to narrative sections, work plan, bibliography, writing sample, and letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear chapter outline and explanation of organization; discuss primary and/or secondary sources and how they will be used; demonstrate familiarity with existing scholarship and how the project’s research base supports the book’s conception and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 4: Quality of the writing sample and clarity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the writing sample and the applicant’s clarity of expression (corresponds to the writing sample and the narrative in its entirety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a sample that demonstrates how the final product will read and ability to appeal to general readers; avoid jargon; the entire narrative and writing sample will be evaluated for clarity. See writing sample guidance for length and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 5: Feasibility, dissemination plan, and likelihood of completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work, the soundness and probable reach of the dissemination plan, and the likelihood that the applicant will complete the project (corresponds to work plan, résumé, publisher’s letter, and letters of reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic schedule, indicate full- or part-time commitment (and fraction if part-time), identify tasks to be completed during award, and explain dissemination/marketing and plans to secure/maintain supplemental digital materials. Explain how project will be completed if manuscript is submitted before award end. Work plan must be feasible and not depend on factors outside applicant control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Applicant type and citizenship/residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be individuals (organizations are ineligible). Eligible individuals must be U.S. citizens or foreign nationals who have lived in the United States or its jurisdictions for at least the three years prior to the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stipend is paid through an institution, the institution must remit all NEH funds to the individual and may not take institutional allowance or claim indirect costs. Foreign nationals who take up permanent residence outside the U.S. between deadline and end of award forfeit eligibility; temporary travel outside U.S. is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Previous publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible you must have either (a) written and published a nonfiction book with a university press or trade press; OR (b) written and published at least three nonfiction articles or essays in general‑interest publications reaching a large national or international audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List relevant publications on résumé with sufficient citation; co‑authored nonfiction book with a university or trade press meets requirement. Exclusions: anthologies, multi‑author edited collections, scholarly editions, translations, dissertations, self‑published books (including presses that require author payment), co‑authored articles, peer‑reviewed academic journal articles, essays in professional publications, transcripts of broadcasts, documentary scripts, podcasts. Unpublished works do not satisfy requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Enrollment and dissertation restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: You are ineligible if you are enrolled in a degree‑granting program at the application deadline or will be during the proposed grant period. You may not request funding for a project based on a completed dissertation or master’s thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply if currently enrolled or if project is primarily a dissertation revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on submissions and concurrent awards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit only one application under this notice. You may revise and resubmit previously rejected applications. You may apply concurrently to certain other NEH individual programs, but you may not accept a Public Scholars award and most other NEH individual awards for the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submit multiple applications, NEH accepts only your last validated submission under the correct funding opportunity. If you accept a Public Scholars award, pending applications for the same project to most other NEH individual programs will be withdrawn. You may hold other non‑NEH fellowships concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of performance must be continuous, begin on the first day of a month and end on the last day of a month, and be the equivalent of six to twelve full‑time months (minimum six, maximum twelve).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing part‑time work, indicate fraction of time; recipients must work at least half time throughout period; NEH will reduce awards to reflect part‑time or shorter commitments; awards cannot exceed 12 months even if part‑time; requesting <6 months will cause rejection. Request a period that suits your schedule; shorter period does not improve chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amounts and stipend policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applicants receive $5,000 per full‑time month; maximum award $60,000 (12 months); minimum award $30,000 (six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will reduce awards to reflect part‑time commitments or periods shorter than 12 months. Awards are outright funds, not contingent on other funding. Indirect costs are unallowable; if paid through an institution, institution must remit all NEH funds to applicant and not take institutional allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will not review incomplete, nonresponsive, or ineligible applications; will not consider applications that exceed page limits or deviate from formatting instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit all required and conditionally required components; do not include unsolicited attachments; missing required documents = no review. Follow deadlines; NEH will not grant deadline extensions for registration issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and file requirements for attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments must be single PDF files, letter size (8.5 x 11), one‑inch margins, font size no smaller than 11‑point, standard Roman fonts (e.g., Arial, Georgia, Helvetica, Times New Roman), single‑spaced (unless guidance says otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations can be any standard citation style and are included in page counts. Name files as specified in the Application Components Table (e.g., narrative.pdf, workplan.pdf, bibliography.pdf, resume.pdf, writingsample.pdf, publisherletter.pdf, delinquentdebt.pdf). Grants.gov will reject files that do not meet technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 1 — Narrative requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative is required, must be succinct, well organized, free of jargon, and limited to three single‑spaced pages; do not include executive summary, cover page, or table of contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided section headings (Appeal and Significance; Sources and organization; Competencies, skills, and access; Final product and dissemination). Include images/charts/footnotes if within three pages. NEH aligned narrative sections with review criteria; clarity of expression is evaluated under Review Criterion 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 2 — Work plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Work plan is required, must present a schedule for the period of performance, indicate months of support requested and fraction of time (full/part), specify where you will work, and identify what parts of the project are already completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work plan must not exceed one page, may be in table form, and must not include material that belongs in the narrative (e.g., detailed chapter outlines or competency discussions). Should not depend on factors outside your control (e.g., receipt of editor comments by a specific date). If previously supported by an NEH Summer Stipend, clearly distinguish tasks supported by each award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 3 — Bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography is required and should list a representative selection of primary and/or secondary sources related to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using archival materials, indicate the archive(s); if sources include interviews, indicate when conducted. Bibliography must not exceed one page. Reviewers use it to assess approach and knowledge of the subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 4 — Résumé requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Résumé is required, must not exceed two pages, and must list the publication(s) used to meet the previous publication requirement with full citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, current and past positions, education (degrees, dates, thesis/dissertation titles), awards/honors with dates, prior NEH support and resulting products, publications and presentations (full citations), languages, and other relevant professional activities. Do not submit a narrative biographical statement; doing so will disqualify the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 5 — Writing sample requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A writing sample is required (NEH strongly recommends a draft chapter or partial chapter of the proposed book); the sample must not exceed twenty PDF pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If typescript, use font no smaller than 11‑point and NEH recommends double‑spacing; single‑spaced samples containing more than the equivalent of twenty double‑spaced pages may not receive full consideration. If reproducing previously published pages, you may include one or two published pages per PDF page; abridgments allowed but must explain omissions. Include headnote if sample is part of proposed book. Sample should demonstrate documentation of sources or explain how sources will be documented. NEH recommends ~7000 words; longer samples may not receive full consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 6 — Publisher’s letter of interest or commitment (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional letter from an official representative of a publisher indicating formats planned, dissemination plans, and print‑run expectations (letter of commitment or interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit a contract, email correspondence, or a letter from an agent; include the letter with other materials by the deadline (cannot be added later). Publisher letters should describe physical formats and dissemination/marketing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 7 — Explanation of delinquent federal debt (conditionally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If delinquent in repayment of federal debt, provide explanation and evidence of repayment agreement and current status; name the file delinquentdebt.pdf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of relevant debt include student loans, taxes, child support, payroll taxes. This attachment is required only for applicants in that situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference policy and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH asks applicants to solicit two letters of reference; provide names, emails, and affiliations on the NEH Supplemental Information form. Letter writers should address the program’s review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 3–4 weeks after the deadline NEH will email letter writers with instructions and deadlines; letters must be submitted online by specified date. Missing letters will not disqualify an application; NEH will add late letters but reviewers may not consider them. Elected government officials, NEH staff, and current National Council members may not serve as letter writers. Publisher letters should not serve as reference letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited project types and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH prohibits support for certain publication types and activities; applications proposing these are subject to disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited items include (but are not limited to): projects by students enrolled in degree programs; revision of dissertations or theses; preparation or revision of textbooks; curriculum development; development of teaching methods or theories; educational or technical impact assessments; guidebooks/how‑to/self‑help books; anthologies and edited collections; works primarily of transcribed interviews/oral histories/questionnaire responses; fiction (including historical fiction), philosophical novels, books for children or young adults, graphic novels/graphic nonfiction; projects whose primary product is a digital archive/database or audiovisual materials; projects devoted primarily to promoting or disseminating a completed book; creation of documentary films; promotion of a particular political/religious/ideological point of view or advocacy of specific policy or legislation; lobbying; projects outside the humanities or that create/perform art rather than humanistic scholarship. Carefully review D6 Funding Restrictions for the full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for public access to products
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH gives preference to projects that provide free access to the public, all else being equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for public access and dissemination; NEH strives to make products available to scholars, educators, students, and the American public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting personal information and human subjects considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If collecting personally identifiable information (PII) or conducting surveys, applicants must protect PII and obtain legally informed consent for survey participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take reasonable and appropriate actions to prevent inadvertent disclosure or data breaches; NEH is not liable for inadvertent disclosures. Obtain informed consent before enrolling participants in surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance, risk assessment, and debarment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will conduct eligibility checks and a risk assessment for selected applications, considering past performance, continued eligibility, and compliance with public policy; awards are subject to NEH terms and federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH may request additional information or place special terms/conditions on awards. NEH will not process awards for individuals with delinquent federal debt or those suspended, debarred, or declared ineligible. Applicants must comply with certification requirements (2 CFR §§ 180.335 and .350).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method, deadlines, and registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted using Grants.gov Workspace under funding opportunity 20241127‑FZ; ensure Grants.gov, login.gov, and SAM.gov registrations are current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will not grant deadline extensions for lack of registration. Follow Grants.gov Workspace procedures, complete required forms, and upload attachments to the Attachments Form. Contact NEH or Grants.gov Applicant Support for technical help and retain case numbers for support calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical and administrative post‑selection requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected, NEH Office of Grant Management will send award documents via eGMS Reach and may require completion of administrative forms and compliance with NEH Public Scholar Program Terms and Conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH may impose special award terms, require additional programmatic or administrative information, and perform further risk management activities prior to issuing funds. Award decisions are discretionary and not appealable.
